# Iásōn at work: mining & natural resources, startups & venture creation, and the myths that got there first
If the stories are true in the way that matters, they should show up in the world without being invoked. **Iásōn** shows up constantly.

The myth of Iásōn is the myth of the quest itself: an unjust king, an impossible errand, a band of heroes, and a prize won by cunning and love rather than by strength alone. Pindar sang it; Apollonius made it an epic; Euripides gave it its dark ending.

The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) — which maps every flagship temple to the industries its archetype demonstrably resonates with, each match argued and open to challenge — seats this temple in **6 industries**. This file reads those seats the way they were earned: through the myths.
## At a Glance

- **Temple:** Iásōn
- **Pantheon:** Greek
- **Domain of influence:** Heroism, the Golden Fleece
- **Pattern seats:** 6
- **Sectors touched:** Energy & Natural World · Commerce & Governance · Culture & Entertainment
- **Strongest seat:** Mining & Natural Resources
- **Series:** The Resonance Files, No. 116 of 271
## The Myth at Work

**The Man with One Sandal.** Pelias, who had seized the throne of Iolkos from Iásōn's father Aisōn, was warned by an oracle to beware the man wearing one sandal.  Iásōn came down from Mount Pelion, where the centaur Cheirōn had reared him, and lost a sandal fording the river Anauros — carrying, Apollodorus says, an old woman who was Hera in disguise. — hold that image; the industries below are where it goes to work.

**The Argo and the Clashing Rocks.** The greatest heroes of the age answered the summons.  The Argo sailed from Pagasai through wonders and losses — Lemnos, the land of women; the death of Hylas, which cost them Heraklēs; the boxing of Polydeukēs with Amykos — until Phineus, the blind seer, told them how to pass the Symplegades, the rocks that clashed together. — that is not just a story. It is a business model, four thousand years early.
## The Seats

Each of these is argued in the atlas with a weight and a why-line. What the atlas cannot fit in one line is the whole myth — so here is each seat with its story restored.

### Mining & Natural Resources

*Extraction, minerals, and subterranean wealth. (Sector: Energy & Natural World)*

The why-line says it in one breath: *The Golden Fleece — gold-seeking to the edge of the map; Strabo records Colchian gold-washing in fleeces.* That is not a resemblance; it is the same act, performed in a newer building.

### Startups & Venture Creation

*Startups, incubators, and venture capital. (Sector: Commerce & Governance)*

*Assembling a legendary team for an audacious expedition — the venture archetype.* — the atlas stops there, out of discipline. The myth keeps going: the function Iásōn performs in the stories is precisely the function this industry sells.

### Gaming, Fantasy & Entertainment IP

*Video games, streaming franchises, and fantasy worlds. (Sector: Culture & Entertainment)*

*Party-assemble quest structure at its mythic source.* — the atlas stops there, out of discipline. The myth keeps going: the function Iásōn performs in the stories is precisely the function this industry sells.

### Leadership, Governance & Public Administration

*Government, executive leadership, and statecraft. (Sector: Commerce & Governance)*

The why-line says it in one breath: *Captaincy of the Argonauts through the Symplegades — expedition leadership.* That is not a resemblance; it is the same act, performed in a newer building.

### Maritime, Shipping & Ocean Industries

*Shipping, ports, fishing, and ocean exploration. (Sector: Energy & Natural World)*

*The Argo's captain; the expedition as a maritime brand.* — the atlas stops there, out of discipline. The myth keeps going: the function Iásōn performs in the stories is precisely the function this industry sells.

The temple holds 1 further seat beyond these — the full, argued list lives on its [patterns floor](/sites/iason/patterns/).

Read the myth again after the seats and it stops sounding ancient: The myth of Iásōn is the myth of the quest itself: an unjust king, an impossible errand, a band of heroes, and a prize won by cunning and love rather than by strength alone. The age changed. The work did not.
## The Method, Stated Plainly

None of this is numerology. A seat exists only where the match can be argued from the deity's documented domains and deeds — weighted, published, and falsifiable. The full derivation, the weights, and the challenge process are public on the [methodology page](/patterns/methodology/). If a seat in this file reads wrong, the atlas itself tells you how to prove it — and the correction becomes part of the record.
## For the Ones Who Work There

If you work in mining & natural resources, startups & venture creation, or any trade this temple holds a seat in, this is the honest version of what a placement means: your industry beside the story it has been re-telling all along — on the temple floor itself, before an audience that came specifically to read it. The [patron tier](/sites/iason/patron/) and the [advertising terms](/terms/advertising/) describe the mechanics; the resonance above describes the fit. The story is the pitch; the seats are just where it already works.
